requirement:
The harness MUST record the sources it supplies to the model, including
mandatory inputs and additional reads, using the evidence input formats
defined by {cite}`requirements.ci.outline_inputs`,
{cite}`requirements.ci.requirements_inputs`, and
{cite}`requirements.definitions.inputs`. The harness MUST create these records
itself so ordinary evidence validation can check them later.
rationale:
I judged the tests adequate for `requirements.authoring.delivered_inputs`. I did not request any implementation source.

Obligations derived from the text:
1. The harness records every source it supplies to the model, both mandatory inputs and additional reads.
2. The records use the outline, requirements and definition input formats.
3. The harness builds the records itself, so ordinary evidence validation can check them later.

Coverage by obligation:
- **Mandatory inputs are recorded.**
  - `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[stdout_emits_only_evidence_json_without_changing_project_files]` runs several determinations.
  - It asserts that the evidence has a requirements input for the subject, a definition input `terms.readiness`, and outline inputs for `src/lib.rs`.
  - `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[ollama_cli_delivers_sources_records_fixme_and_keeps_usage_content_free]` asserts a mandatory outline input for `fn[ready_test]` and the `terms.readiness` definition.
- **Outline format.**
  - `stdout_emits_only_evidence_json_without_changing_project_files` asserts that outline inputs have exactly the keys `file`, `hash` and `item`.
  - `src/authoring/tools.rs#fn[reading_records_only_delivered_sources_and_their_terms]` compares recorded inputs with `crate::inputs::outline_input`.
  - `src/authoring/tools.rs#fn[line_range_reads_record_the_innermost_covering_nodes]` records the innermost covering node and asserts that it has no `line_start` or `text`.
- **Requirements and definition formats.** `src/authoring/tools.rs#fn[declaration_text_reaches_the_model_redacted]` does the following for both a `requirements` read and a `definition` read:
  - It asserts the input shape: `requirements`, `matches` and `text` for requirements, and `definition` and `text` for definitions.
  - It asserts that the terms the read delivers (`definitions`) are recorded together with the input.
  - It asserts that the recorded inputs equal the delivered ones, and that a repeated delivery is recorded once.
- **Additional reads.**
  - The Ollama CLI test covers `habeas` line-range reads and a repeated read.
  - The repeated read is recorded once.
  - The recorded `extra.txt` inputs equal `habeas::outline_inputs_for_lines`.
  - Failed reads (`absent.txt`), `list_files` and `ripgrep` locations are not recorded.
  - The Bedrock CLI test checks the same recording for a line-range read.
  - `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[implementation_discovery_has_no_text_or_evidence_until_the_model_requests_a_read]` shows that `references` discovery records nothing. After a read, the `fn[ready]` input is recorded exactly once, with matching file, item and hash.
- **Only delivered sources are recorded.**
  - `src/authoring/mod.rs#fn[only_inputs_on_delivered_pages_are_recorded]` shows that when results are paged, only inputs on delivered pages are recorded. The recorded set is exactly the prefix of delivered items.
  - `src/authoring/pages.rs#fn[paged_inputs_carry_their_definitions_and_deliver_only_their_own_inputs]` checks the same per page, including each page's definitions.
- **Harness-created and checkable by ordinary validation.**
  - The records come from the harness's own `record_inputs`. The model supplies only tool arguments.
  - The Ollama CLI test runs `habeas::validate_repository` on the written evidence and finds no error for it.
  - The same test then shows that a record with a false determination is rejected, so the validation is real.
- **Live test.** `tests/live_bedrock.rs#fn[live_bedrock_authoring]` also asserts that a model-read file appears as an outline input with only a hash and no text. It is skipped in CI.

The cited input-format requirements (`requirements.ci.outline_inputs`, `requirements.ci.requirements_inputs`, `requirements.definitions.inputs`) are context here. Their own validation rules are not reassessed.

I found no unacknowledged gap.

text: :::{req} delivered_inputs
The harness MUST record the sources it supplies to the model, including
mandatory inputs and additional reads, using the evidence input formats
defined by {cite}`requirements.ci.outline_inputs`,
{cite}`requirements.ci.requirements_inputs`, and
{cite}`requirements.definitions.inputs`. The harness MUST create these records
itself so ordinary evidence validation can check them later.
:::{req} outline_inputs
For an outline input, Habeas MUST parse `file` with its language's grammar under
{cite}`requirements.references.outlines` and resolve `item` to exactly one
outline node under {cite}`requirements.references.outline_selectors`. It MUST
compare `hash` with the node's current structural hash under
{cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`. It MUST derive the node's
inclusive line range, including attached comments and attributes, during
validation for display and reference coverage. Moving the node, editing other
nodes, or editing comments its profile does not hash MUST NOT invalidate the
input. Habeas MUST report a missing file, unsupported language, parse failure,
invalid or ambiguous selector, or changed hash.
:::{req} requirements_inputs

For a requirements input, `requirements` MUST be a {term}`requirements.references.definition_selection`, and Habeas MUST match it against all defined requirements and named examples. It MUST recompute the matches during validation, sort their full names, and compare them with `matches`. It MUST take each match's complete raw fenced declaration, including its opening and closing lines, concatenate those declarations in full-name order with one blank line between them, and compare the resulting raw lines with `text`. It MUST retain every match's current source file and inclusive line range for display and reference coverage. A selection matching no definitions MUST be invalid. Adding, removing, renaming, or changing a matched definition MUST invalidate the stored input; moving an unchanged declaration within the book MUST NOT. Errors MUST identify the selection and affected definitions when available.
:::{req} inputs

Evidence inputs MAY have a definition form containing exactly `definition` and `text`. `definition` MUST identify one named definition; `text` MUST contain its complete raw fenced declaration as source lines, including its phrase option and explanatory body.

Validation MUST reject missing definitions and changed snapshot text, identifying the definition and showing a compact diff when available. Moving an unchanged definition within its chapter MUST NOT invalidate its snapshot. Evidence displays MUST show the definition name, current source location, and recorded text.
:::{definition} definition_selection
:phrase: definition selection
A full requirement or example name, or a definition glob, identifying the
requirements and named examples it matches under
{cite}`requirements.references.definition_globs`. A name without `*` selects
exactly that definition.
